message.content: The description model is already recorded and there are no open description tasks. That sharpens the risk analysis behind claims c1/c2 without asserting a verdict.

message.reasoning_content: No new description tasks. The description model is already recorded. I could add a refinement: per-term midpoint error for high-f terms. Actually note: midpoint quadrature error for a single sinusoid isn't O(|a|); aliased frequencies near multiples of 32*2π dominate. Actually a key analytical insight: 32-point midpoint rule for sin(f t + φ) gives exact average of aliased frequency f' = f mod 64π? The discrete sum of e^{i f t_j} over 32 midpoints is zero unless f ≈ m·64π. So the midpoint estimate for the sinusoid terms is ≈0 (exactly 1 + small residue), while reference contribution per term is ≤ |a|/f ≤ 0.1/0.5 = 0.2. Reference ≈ 1 + sum of a_k*(cos φ - cos(φ+f))/f. Since 64π ≈ 201, frequencies up to 220: terms near 201±small produce near-resonance errors. Also low-frequency terms contribute up to ~0.2 each. That's a concrete refinement worth recording for the Skeptic/Experimenter: error per row ≈ |sum of reference contributions of oscillatory terms|, relative error could be up to ~ (8·0.2)/... hmm reference norm could be ~0.5-1.
